question: In heart failure, sustained activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) and sympathetic nervous system is initially compensatory but ultimately becomes maladaptive, leading to progressive cardiac remodelling.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The initial RAAS/SNS activation maintains perfusion but chronic neurohormonal excess causes cardiomyocyte loss and fibrosis. Blocking these pathways (ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, MRAs, SGLT2 inhibitors) is the basis of evidence-based HFrEF management.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The short-term haemodynamic rescue (increased preload, afterload, and inotropy) becomes harmful over time: catecholamines cause myocyte apoptosis, angiotensin II drives fibrosis, and aldosterone causes sodium retention — all worsening ventricular remodelling. This is the neurohormonal model underpinning all four pillars of HFrEF therapy.
